newsitem.title: UK: Oil price slumps as bull run hits brick wall.
newsitem.headline: Oil price slumps as bull run hits brick wall.

text.p: World oil prices went into a steep decline on Thursday, finally breaking the back of a four-and-a-half month bull run which took crude markets to levels not seen for nearly six years.
December futures for benchmark oil North Sea Brent blend finished down 88 cents a barrel at $22.69 a barrel.
The slide was led by a change in sentiment on U.S. markets where crude and gasoline led the way lower.
But dealers said news that two rival Kurdish factions had agreed to extend a U.S. brokered ceasefire in northern Iraq has also undermined the market.
"This is meltdown," said broker Tim Holmes at MeesPierson Derivatives in London. "It's more than your average correction."
Holmes said the selloff confirmed that crude had said farewell, in the short-term at least, to the highs which took Brent above $25 a barrel in mid-October.
Dealers said big financial hedge funds helped drive prices lower on Thursday as local speculators on the New York Mercantile Exchange sparked computerised stop-loss sell orders.
"We went through some important technical stops and that triggered some hedge fund selling," said a futures broker.
Brent peaked two weeks ago at $25.06 a barrel, a $7.50 rise in little more than four months, but has since shed a third of that value.
Dealers said weakness on the market for gasoline in the U.S., reversing some gains of earlier in the week, also undermined oil on Thursday.
"Gasoline stopped the rot yesterday and it's gasoline which is taking us down today," said a broker.
In Ankara, U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau said rival Kurdish groups had agreed to extend a ceasefire in northern Iraq with a view to making it permanent.
A U.N. oil-for-food exchange was put on hold at the end of August when clashes made it unsafe for UN monitors in the region.
"I suppose this puts oil-for-food back on the map but that's not the real reason this market came off," said a dealer in London.
"Basically the market lost its nerve."

Thursday's slide followed losses earlier in the week in response to inventory data from the United States showing the start of a build in heating oil stocks in the world's biggest oil consuming nation.
Brent markets shrugged off news on Thursday that production was halted at Norway's 250,000 barrel a day Heidrun oilfield because of technical problems.
